summary: Number 30 of South Korean Interim Government Activities covers March 1948, bound in a Google Books volume with Nos. 31 (April) and 32 (May). It reports a turbulent month: Korean politics divided over the UN-observed 10 May election in the south, communist-inspired riots under a South Korea Labor Party plan captured by police, a wildcat Seoul Electric strike, and Kim Koo and Kimm Kiu-sic's exchange with Pyongyang leaders over a joint conference. Administrative items include Ordinance No. 176 (protection from unlawful arrest), creation of the National Land Administration to sell former Japanese farmland, and formation of the National Election Committee. Economic sections give detailed tables on prices, industrial production, coal, trade, finance, transport and labor, with prices softening and imports exceeding exports. Historians will find useful the National Economic Board statistics, FY 1948/49 aid planning, refugee flows, Mukden repatriation planning, and press and youth-group reports.
highlights: Ordinance No. 176, effective 1 April, gave Koreans protection against unlawful arrest and set time allowances for prisoners, while Ordinance No. 174 of 22 March created the National Land Administration and dissolved the New Korea Company.

A South Korea Labor Party riot master plan was seized, with attacks on police boxes, Chinhae city hall burned, and 41 arrests in Kyongsang-namdo, as Korean politics split over the UN-observed 10 May election.
Seoul Electric Company workers struck without authorization from 13 March, halting Seoul streetcars 12-17 March; Declaration No. 6 declared the strike unlawful on 15 March.
Southbound refugee flow rose nearly 200 percent over February, and a plan was drawn up to fly 2,000 Korean leaders from Mukden to Tientsin and ship them to Inchon.

Kim Koo and Kimm Kiu-sic wrote to Kim Il-sung and Kim Doo-bong in Pyongyang; North Korea accepted a joint conference and suggested 14 April, while Kimm Kiu-sic's Assembly resignation was accepted 2 March.
February flour output rose 123 percent and paper 73.6 percent, anthracite quota rose to 76,000 tons, and bituminous coal imports from Japan reached 75,243 tons in March.
Private imports of 625.9 million won exceeded exports of 384.4 million, about 95 percent of exports going to Hong Kong; Seoul retail prices fell, cleaned rice down nearly seven percent.
Korean National Youth reported 646,331 members, and 2,151,740 members worked 75,289,176 volunteer hours in 15 months, amid opposition from rightist and leftist groups.

sections.summary: Registration closed 9 April with 7,730,000 voters (over 94 percent), 13,407 polling places and 942 candidates; Military Government personnel 3,041.

sections.title: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: KILA met once, on 19 April, enacted nothing and voted a 30-day adjournment, tantamount to dissolution; summary lists its 11 Public Acts.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: Pyongyang North-South conference (19-30 April) attended by Kimm Kiu-sic and Kim Koo; 939 candidates; Choi Nung-chin challenged Rhee's seat.

sections.title: Legal Affairs
sections.summary: Ordinances 182-191; election postponed to 10 May; tax exemption raised to 25,000 won; Hodge's 11-point Proclamation of Rights; Judge Lobingier's proposed Korean Civil Code.

sections.title: National Police
sections.summary: Police resented warrant rules and release of over 3,000 offenders; about 52 of 13,455 booths attacked; Cheju-do riots from 3 April with about 2,000 rebels.

sections.title: Interzone Activities
sections.summary: Mail exchange weekly from 15 April (59,000 pieces versus 37,000 in March); Radio Pyongyang promoted the 30 April constitution; 21 Koreans killed at the border.

sections.title: No. 31 Part VI: Social
sections.summary: April social affairs: cholera immunization, Mukden repatriation ship, literacy figures, Arbor Day, press on the Pyongyang conference, Korean National Youth at 774,949 members, and women's election work.

sections.title: Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Cholera vaccination continued; refugee ship sailed for Mukden repatriates 30 April; 520,000 pounds of DDT; 10,053 low-cost housing units.

sections.title: Education
sections.summary: Literacy rose from 21 to 71 percent (1945-47); department staff cut from 177 to 143; 13,230,670 textbooks printed since 1945.

sections.title: Culture
sections.summary: Arbor Day 5 April, 100,000,000 trees planted; 58 Olympic athletes selected for London after $140,000 raised; Suh Yun-bok won the trials.

sections.title: Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: Papers focused on the Pyongyang conference and 10 May election (91.7 percent registration, 939 candidates); Cheju riots and closed Korean schools in Japan.

sections.title: Korean National Youth, Inc.
sections.summary: On 5 April 67,475 members planted 3,451,300 trees; membership 774,949 by 30 April; 62 training centers; 36,599 leaders trained.

sections.title: Women's Activities
sections.summary: Husband fined 5,000 won for slapping his wife; Women's Bureau gave over 50 election talks and issued 5,000 magazines; profile of the Koh sisters.

sections.title: Bound issue: No. 32, May 1948
sections.summary: Separate report bound into the volume (May 1948): cover, contents, summary of the 10 May election and power cutoff, and Parts I-VI; not part of No. 30.

sections.title: No. 32 front matter and summary
sections.summary: Roster (Chairman Wilhelm Anderson), contents and May summary: 10 May election (91 percent turnout), 31 May Assembly seating, 14 May North Korean power cutoff cutting output 75 percent.

sections.title: No. 32 Part I: Basic Aspects
sections.summary: South Korean population 20,041,000 by January 1948; net migration 1,534,000; first Mukden repatriates (3,831); vested property: 2,334 statements.

sections.title: No. 32 Part II: Production and Supply
sections.summary: May production and supply: drought threatening the 673,982-ton summer grain forecast, rising prices, 75 percent output loss from the 14 May power cutoff, and settled Pusan and Seoul strikes.

sections.title: Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
sections.summary: 5 May forecast of 673,982 metric tons on 1,956,227 acres; fertilizer received 358,776 tons since July 1947; NLA had sold 448,513 farms (76 percent) by 31 May.

sections.title: Prices
sections.summary: Seoul wholesale prices rose in May, cleaned rice up nearly 10 percent; retail prices rose after the March-April dip; rice controlled at 280 won per large mal.

sections.title: Industrial Production
sections.summary: Rubber shoes 2,261,906 pairs in April; cigarettes up 66.2 percent; after the 14 May power cutoff, May paper fell 61.7 percent, cement stopped.

sections.title: Mining and Minerals
sections.summary: Anthracite 68,612 tons in April, up 9.3 percent; mines sought a 200,000,000 won loan; May bituminous imports 61,068 tons; Ongjin and Haeju mines flooded.

sections.title: Allocations and Distribution
sections.summary: 6,936,921 liters of gasoline allocated for elections and farming; salt distribution 27,434 tons; ex-Japanese materials passed to Bureau of Industry 15 May.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: April private imports 746,144,000 won, exports 390,741,000 won, over 99 percent to Hong Kong; FLC purchases about $971,000.

sections.title: Labor
sections.summary: Tai Han Union sought a closed shop at Seoul Electric; 450 Pusan stevedores struck 11-12 May, leading to a joint hiring hall and a 70-30 fee split.

sections.title: No. 32 Part III: Public Services
sections.summary: Communist sabotage around the 10 May election, power delivery cut to 56.1 million KWH by the 14 May cutoff, and a Public Works review of two and a half years' work.

sections.title: Transportation
sections.summary: Sabotage wrecked a passenger train near Mokpo; coal 42.9 percent of shipping priority; April revenue 374,580,000 won; locomotives operable 264; 2,308 Tientsin refugees handled.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: Arson destroyed Yongdungpo repeater station 23 May, killing two employees and a policeman; employment 12,761; phone and telegraph rates raised to about 85 times 1937 levels.

sections.title: Public Utilities
sections.summary: May deliveries fell to 56.1 million KWH after the 14 May cutoff; Daylight Saving Time from 31 May; Seoul streetcars resumed within 45 minutes.

sections.title: Public Works
sections.summary: Two and a half years of work reviewed: 162 kilometers of levees, 515 pieces of heavy equipment distributed, 153 million won flood-control subsidies, 181 fires.

sections.title: No. 32 Part IV: Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Chosun note issue 28.6 billion won; overdraft 20,232 million; April revenue 1,930 million, tobacco 702 million; deposits a record 56,421 million won; loans down 2,096 million.

sections.title: No. 32 Part V: Government and Politics
sections.summary: 10 May election chose 198 Assembly members; Rhee Syngman Speaker 31 May; 25-130 percent civil service pay rise; Court Reorganization Ordinance 192; 31 border incidents.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: Chief Adviser Edgar Johnson held 72 conferences in Washington, returning 25 May; 25-130 percent pay rise from 1 June; Military Government personnel 3,003.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: Over 91 percent of registrants voted and 198 members were returned; Rhee elected Speaker with 188 votes at the 31 May opening; Cheju-do voting postponed in two districts.

sections.title: Legal Affairs
sections.summary: Ordinances 192-197, chiefly Court Reorganization separating courts from Justice from 1 June; prison population 22,141 at 30 April; Property Claims screening began 22 May.

sections.title: National Police
sections.summary: Four candidates and 32 policemen killed in May; 68 of 13,407 booths attacked on 10 May; Cheju-do 3,126 held and about 600 casualties.

sections.title: Interzone Activities
sections.summary: Thirty-one border incidents, mostly near the Oe-Dong dam; Soviet Yak-9 landed near Yosu 19 May; over 43,000 pieces of mail exchanged, down from 59,000.

sections.title: No. 32 Part VI: Social
sections.summary: May social affairs: Mukden repatriation, UNRRA welfare grants, education ordinances, 845 teachers in summer training, election culture, press on the power cutoff, KNY at 859,208 members, and women voters.

sections.title: Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Mukden repatriation ships carried 1,091, 1,240 and 1,070 people through Inchon quarantine; 2,106 low-cost housing units completed in Kyongsang-namdo; UNRRA funds to five projects.

sections.title: Education
sections.summary: Three draft ordinances for school districts and household-tax financing; 1948/49 budget 1,500,000,000 won; 845 teachers for summer session; 13,888,351 textbooks published since 1945.

sections.title: Culture
sections.summary: Election campaign teams gave 803 performances to 1,334,464 people; US Information Center opened in Seoul; Rhee exhibition drew 100,000; KBS ran 44 election programs.

sections.title: Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: Press debated the Pyongyang Conference, election, 14 May cutoff and Assembly opening; 202 dead and 643 wounded from 31 March to 17 May; Country Guard Corps disbanded 22 May.

sections.title: Korean National Youth, Inc.
sections.summary: Thirty-three KNY members won Assembly seats against 13 for Dai Dong; membership 859,208 at end of May; 65 training centers; 1948/49 budget 20,600,000 won.

sections.title: Women's Activities
sections.summary: About 3,000,000 women voted on 10 May (49.4 percent of registrants); 19 ran for the Assembly and none won; Ewha University marked its 62nd anniversary.
